audio_cues.text: I was 28 when Dev held up my pay stub and asked me one question.
"Who's keeping the difference?"
Then he pointed at one line, and my stomach dropped.
For three years, I'd been turning down free money.
Twenty-five.
First real job.
Forty-four thousand a year, and I felt like I'd made it.
So I did what felt right and leased a brand-new car, four hundred and eighty-nine dollars a month.
Somewhere on page six it said the company would match every dollar I put into my retirement plan, up to four percent of my salary.
I picked two percent, because two sounded responsible, and the lease sounded urgent.
I put in two, so they put in two.
The other two percent?
It wasn't saved for later.
It just never got paid.
That was eight hundred and eighty dollars the first year.
I went home, opened the app on my phone, and changed two to four.
It took ninety seconds.
Ninety seconds, three years late.
You don't have to max it out.
You just don't want to skip the free part.
Before you cut a single thing, collect what you're already owed.
